author: high
claim: For each nonnegative integer k, the target sum counts binary words of length 2k+1 in which H is the strict-majority symbol, classified by the position of the (k+1)-st H.
evidence: Fix k. If the (k+1)-st H occurs after exactly j occurrences of T, then 0<=j<=k. Before that final H there are k H's and j T's, which can be arranged in binom(k+j,j) ways. After it there remain (2k+1)-(k+j+1)=k-j arbitrary positions, giving 2^(k-j) choices. Thus this class has 2^(k-j) binom(k+j,j) words, and summing j=0,...,k counts all H-majority words exactly once. Swapping H and T is a fixed-point-free pairing between H-majority and T-majority words of odd length 2k+1, so exactly half of the 2^(2k+1) words are H-majority, namely 2^(2k)=4^k.

links.statement: The left-hand side equals the number of H-majority binary words of length 2k+1.

glossary.H: one of two symbols in a binary word
glossary.T: the other symbol in a binary word
glossary.j: the number of T symbols before the (k+1)-st H
